chapter_text:
CHAPTER 4 — वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् (VACHAM MANDANAM SATYAM)

भूमिका (Introduction)

What truly adorns a human being? Gold armlets, pearl necklaces, perfumes, fine clothes? The Sanskrit poets answer with one voice: none of these. The real ornament of a person is his or her वाणी (speech) — and the real ornament of speech itself is सत्यम् (truth). This is the meaning of the chapter's title, वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् — 'truth is the ornament of speech'. वाचाम् is the genitive plural of वाक् (speech), and मण्डनम् means ornament or decoration; so the phrase literally says 'of (all) words, the true decoration is truth'.

In this lesson (NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit, Course 309) we study the ethics and the beauty of speech through famous public-domain verses drawn from भर्तृहरि's नीतिशतकम्, the मनुस्मृतिः, चाणक्यनीतिः, the श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता and the विदुरनीतिः of the महाभारतम्. Together they teach four ideals of noble speech: (1) सत्यम् — truthfulness; (2) माधुर्यम् — sweetness (मधुरा वाणी); (3) हितम् — helpfulness, speaking for the good of the listener; and (4) संयमः — restraint, the discipline of avoiding harsh (कठोर), false (अनृत) and hurtful words. For each verse we give the शब्दार्थ (word meanings), the अन्वय (prose word-order), an English translation and the भावः (message), and at the end we draw grammar — सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and लकार — from the verses themselves.

मुख्यश्लोकाः (The core verses)

1) केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः
   न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः ।
   वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते
   क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥ (भर्तृहरिः, नीतिशतकम्)
   शब्दार्थ: केयूराणि = armlets, bracelets worn on the upper arm; न भूषयन्ति = do not adorn; पुरुषम् = a person; हाराः = necklaces; चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः = shining bright like the moon; स्नानम् = bathing; विलेपनम् = sandal-paste, perfumed unguent; कुसुमम् = flower; अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः = well-dressed hair; वाणी एका = speech alone; समलङ्करोति = fully adorns; या = which; संस्कृता = refined, polished, cultured; धार्यते = is maintained, is borne; क्षीयन्ते = wear away, perish; खलु = indeed; भूषणानि = ornaments; सततम् = always, forever; वाग्भूषणम् = the ornament of speech; भूषणम् = the (real) ornament.
   अन्वय: केयूराणि पुरुषं न भूषयन्ति, चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः हाराः न (भूषयन्ति), न स्नानम्, न विलेपनम्, न कुसुमम्, न अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः (भूषयन्ति)। या संस्कृता (वाणी) धार्यते, (सा) एका वाणी पुरुषं समलङ्करोति। भूषणानि खलु क्षीयन्ते; वाग्भूषणं सततं भूषणम्।
   Translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor moon-bright necklaces; neither bath nor sandal-paste, neither flowers nor elegantly dressed hair. Speech alone, when it is kept refined and cultured, truly adorns a person. All (other) ornaments wear away; the ornament of speech is the ornament forever.
   भावः (Message): External decorations are borrowed and perishable — they fade, break and go out of fashion. Cultured, truthful, gentle speech is an inner ornament that no thief can steal and no time can tarnish. This verse of भर्तृहरि gives the chapter its central idea: वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्.

2) सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् ।
   प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः ॥ (मनुस्मृतिः 4.138)
   शब्दार्थ: सत्यम् = truth; ब्रूयात् = one should speak; प्रियम् = what is pleasant, agreeable; न ब्रूयात् = one should not speak; अप्रियम् = unpleasant, hurtful; च = and; अनृतम् = falsehood, untruth; एषः = this; धर्मः = law, duty; सनातनः = eternal, ancient.
   अन्वय: सत्यं ब्रूयात्, प्रियं ब्रूयात्, (किन्तु) अप्रियं सत्यं न ब्रूयात्, प्रियम् अनृतं च न ब्रूयात् — एषः सनातनः धर्मः।
   Translation: Speak the truth, speak what is pleasant; do not speak a truth that is (needlessly) hurtful, and do not speak a falsehood merely because it pleases — this is the eternal law.
   भावः: मनु gives a fourfold rule that balances सत्यम् with माधुर्यम्. Truth without kindness can wound; sweetness without truth becomes flattery and lying. Noble speech must be BOTH true AND kind. When a truth can only hurt and cannot help, silence or gentle rewording is better; but a pleasing lie is never permitted.

3) प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः ।
   तस्मात्तदेव वक्तव्यं वचने का दरिद्रता ॥ (चाणक्यनीतिः)
   शब्दार्थ: प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन = by the giving of pleasant words; सर्वे = all; तुष्यन्ति = are pleased, satisfied; जन्तवः = living beings; तस्मात् = therefore; तत् एव = that alone; वक्तव्यम् = should be spoken; वचने = in speech; का = what; दरिद्रता = poverty, miserliness.
   अन्वय: प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे जन्तवः तुष्यन्ति। तस्मात् तत् एव वक्तव्यम्। वचने का दरिद्रता?
   Translation: By the gift of pleasant words all living beings are made happy. Therefore pleasant words alone should be spoken — why be a miser in speech?
   भावः: Kind words cost nothing, yet they are a real दानम् (gift) that delights every creature. Being rude is a strange sort of poverty — a poverty of the tongue in a person who may otherwise be rich. चाणक्य asks: since sweetness in speech is free, why hoard it?

4) अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
   स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥ (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 17.15)
   शब्दार्थ: अनुद्वेगकरम् = not causing agitation or distress; वाक्यम् = speech, sentence; सत्यम् = true; प्रियहितम् = pleasant and beneficial; च = and; यत् = which; स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् = the regular practice of self-study / recitation of the scriptures; एव = indeed; वाङ्मयम् = consisting of speech, verbal; तपः = austerity, discipline; उच्यते = is called.
   अन्वय: यत् वाक्यम् अनुद्वेगकरं सत्यं प्रियहितं च (अस्ति), स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं च एव — (एतत्) वाङ्मयं तपः उच्यते।
   Translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is true, pleasant and beneficial, and (along with it) the regular practice of self-study — this is called the austerity of speech (वाङ्मयं तपः).
   भावः: The गीता raises speech to the level of तपस् (spiritual discipline). Four marks define disciplined speech: अनुद्वेगकरम् (it disturbs no one), सत्यम् (it is true), प्रियम् (it is pleasant) and हितम् (it is beneficial). Add to these स्वाध्याय (daily study), and the tongue itself becomes an instrument of tapas. Speech-discipline is thus not merely etiquette but self-cultivation.

5) हस्तस्य भूषणं दानं सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् ।
   श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं शास्त्रं भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम् ॥ (सुभाषितम्)
   शब्दार्थ: हस्तस्य = of the hand; भूषणम् = ornament; दानम् = charity, giving; सत्यम् = truth; कण्ठस्य = of the throat / voice; श्रोत्रस्य = of the ear; शास्त्रम् = learning, sacred knowledge; भूषणैः = with (other) ornaments; किम् = what; प्रयोजनम् = use, purpose.
   अन्वय: हस्तस्य भूषणं दानम्, कण्ठस्य भूषणं सत्यम्, श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं शास्त्रम् — (अन्यैः) भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम्?
   Translation: The ornament of the hand is charity; the ornament of the throat is truth; the ornament of the ear is learning — what use, then, of (other) ornaments?
   भावः: For every limb the poets prescribe a moral jewel: the hand shines by giving, the voice by truth, the ear by listening to wisdom. The verse repeats the chapter's title-idea in miniature — सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् is simply वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् said of the throat.

6) रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् ।
   वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् ॥ (विदुरनीतिः, महाभारतम्)
   शब्दार्थ: रोहते = grows again, heals; सायकैः = by arrows; विद्धम् = pierced; वनम् = forest; परशुना = by an axe; हतम् = cut down, struck; वाचा = by speech; दुरुक्तम् = ill-spoken, harsh; बीभत्सम् = ugly, cruel; न संरोहति = does not heal over; वाक्क्षतम् = a wound made by words.
   अन्वय: सायकैः विद्धं (शरीरं) रोहते, परशुना हतं वनं (अपि) रोहते; (किन्तु) वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं वाक्क्षतं न संरोहति।
   Translation: A body pierced by arrows heals; even a forest cut down by the axe grows again; but the ugly wound made by a harshly spoken word never heals.
   भावः: This is the dark side of the power of speech. Physical wounds close; forests regrow; but a cruel word lodges in the heart forever. विदुर therefore counsels perfect restraint (संयमः) of the tongue — think before speaking, for a word once released, like an arrow, cannot be recalled.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the verses

(A) सन्धिः (Sandhi). Joins and splits drawn from the verses:
  • चन्द्र + उज्ज्वलाः → चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः (अ + उ = ओ, गुणसन्धिः).
  • न + अलङ्कृताः → नालङ्कृताः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः); similarly न + अनृतम् → नानृतम्.
  • वाक् + भूषणम् → वाग्भूषणम् (क् before a voiced sound becomes ग् — जश्त्वसन्धिः); compare वाक् + मयम् → वाङ्मयम् (क् before the nasal म becomes ङ् — अनुनासिकसन्धिः/परसवर्णः).
  • सत्यम् + अप्रियम् → सत्यमप्रियम् (simple joining of म् with the following vowel).
  • तस्मात् + तत् + एव → तस्मात्तदेव (त् + त् double; तत् + एव = तदेव, त् becomes द् before the vowel).
  • च + एव → चैव (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धिः).
  • तपः + उच्यते → तप उच्यते (विसर्गलोपः — the visarga is dropped before the vowel उ).
  • सायकैः + विद्धम् → सायकैर्विद्धम् (विसर्गसन्धिः — visarga becomes र् before a voiced consonant).
  Being able to perform सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting) of forms like वाग्भूषणम्, नालङ्कृताः, चैव and तस्मात्तदेव is an essential senior-secondary skill.

(B) समासः (Compounds).
  • वाग्भूषणम् = वाचः भूषणम् — 'the ornament OF speech' — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः.
  • प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन = प्रियस्य वाक्यस्य प्रदानेन — 'by the giving of pleasant words' — a chain built on तत्पुरुष compounding (प्रियवाक्य itself is कर्मधारयः: प्रियं च तत् वाक्यं च).
  • अनुद्वेगकरम् = न उद्वेगकरम् — 'NOT causing agitation' — नञ्समासः (the negative अन्- before a vowel).
  • प्रियहितम् = प्रियं च हितं च — 'pleasant and beneficial' — द्वन्द्वसमासः.
  • वाक्क्षतम् = वाचा क्षतम् — 'a wound (made) by speech' — तृतीयातत्पुरुषसमासः.
  • वाङ्मयम् is not a समास but a तद्धित form: वाक् + मयट् (the suffix मय, 'consisting of').

(C) विभक्तिः (Cases) — roles played by words in the verses:
  • प्रथमा (nominative — subject): हाराः, वाणी, भूषणानि, जन्तवः, धर्मः.
  • द्वितीया (accusative — object): पुरुषम् ('adorns THE PERSON'), सत्यम्/प्रियम् (objects of ब्रूयात्).
  • तृतीया (instrumental — by/with): प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन 'by the gift of kind words', सायकैः 'by arrows', परशुना 'by an axe', वाचा 'by speech', भूषणैः 'with ornaments'.
  • षष्ठी (genitive — of): वाचाम् 'of words' (in the title), हस्तस्य, कण्ठस्य, श्रोत्रस्य.
  • सप्तमी (locative — in): वचने 'in speech' (वचने का दरिद्रता).

(D) लकारः and verb-forms:
  • लट् लकारः (present tense): भूषयन्ति, समलङ्करोति, क्षीयन्ते, तुष्यन्ति, रोहते, संरोहति.
  • विधिलिङ् लकारः (optative — 'should'): ब्रूयात् 'one should speak' (from the root ब्रू).
  • कर्मवाच्यम् (passive voice): धार्यते 'is maintained', उच्यते 'is called'.
  • कृत्यप्रत्ययः (gerundive of obligation): वक्तव्यम् 'ought to be spoken' (वच् + तव्यत्).

सारांशः (Summary)

The chapter वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् gathers the classical Sanskrit teaching on speech. भर्तृहरि declares that armlets, necklaces, baths, perfumes and flowers cannot adorn a person — only refined speech can, for all other ornaments perish while वाग्भूषणम् lasts forever. मनु frames the eternal fourfold rule: speak the truth, speak sweetly, avoid the needlessly hurtful truth and never utter a pleasing lie. चाणक्य reminds us that kind words are a free gift that delights all beings — why be a miser in speech? The गीता defines the austerity of speech (वाङ्मयं तपः) by four marks — non-agitating, true, pleasant, beneficial — plus daily self-study. A सुभाषित assigns each limb its true jewel: charity for the hand, truth for the throat, learning for the ear. And विदुर warns of the other side: wounds of arrows and axes heal, but the wound of a cruel word (वाक्क्षतम्) never does. From these verses we also learned सन्धि (चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः, वाग्भूषणम्, चैव), समास (षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, नञ्, द्वन्द्व), the common विभक्ति roles, and verb-forms (ब्रूयात् विधिलिङ्, उच्यते कर्मवाच्य, वक्तव्यम् gerundive). The lesson for life is simple: let every word be true, sweet, useful and restrained — for truth is the ornament of speech, and speech is the lasting ornament of the human being.

topics.name: वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् — Theme and Introduction
topics.description: The meaning of the title phrase 'truth is the ornament of speech' (वाचाम् genitive plural of वाक्; मण्डनम् = ornament) and the chapter's four ideals of noble speech — सत्यम् (truthfulness), माधुर्यम् (sweetness), हितम् (benefit) and संयमः (restraint).

topics.name: वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् — Speech as the True Ornament (Bhartrhari)
topics.description: भर्तृहरि's नीतिशतकम् verse केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम्... — external ornaments (armlets, necklaces, bath, sandal-paste, flowers, dressed hair) perish, while refined and cultured speech (संस्कृता वाणी) is the lasting ornament of a person.

topics.name: सत्यं च प्रियं च — Truth with Sweetness (Manu and Chanakya)
topics.description: मनुस्मृति's fourfold rule सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात्... balancing truth with kindness, and चाणक्य's प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः — pleasant words are a free gift that delights all beings (वचने का दरिद्रता).

topics.name: वाङ्मयं तपः — The Discipline of Speech (Gita 17.15)
topics.description: The भगवद्गीता's definition of the austerity of speech: वाक्यम् that is अनुद्वेगकरम् (non-agitating), सत्यम् (true), प्रियम् (pleasant) and हितम् (beneficial), together with स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् (daily self-study), is वाङ्मयं तपः.

topics.name: दुर्वचनं वाक्क्षतम् — The Wound of Harsh Words
topics.description: विदुरनीति's warning रोहते सायकैर्विद्धम्... — wounds of arrows and the axe heal, but the wound made by a harsh word (वाक्क्षतम्) never heals; hence the need for perfect restraint (संयमः) of the tongue. Includes the सुभाषित हस्तस्य भूषणं दानम्... on the moral jewel of each limb.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the Verses (सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति, लकार)
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the verses: गुण/दीर्घ/वृद्धि/जश्त्व/विसर्ग सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद (चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः, वाग्भूषणम्, नालङ्कृताः, चैव); समास types (षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, नञ्, द्वन्द्व); विभक्ति roles; and verb-forms — लट्, विधिलिङ् (ब्रूयात्), passive (उच्यते), gerundive (वक्तव्यम्).

chapter_summary.title: वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् (Vacham Mandanam Satyam) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 4 on the ethics and beauty of speech. Through verses of भर्तृहरि, मनु, चाणक्य, the गीता and विदुर it teaches that truth is the ornament of speech, that words must be true, sweet, beneficial and restrained, and it draws सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and लकार from the verses.

branches.label: शीर्षकार्थः — The title
details: वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् = truth is the ornament of speech

branches.label: सत्यं च प्रियं च — Manu & Chanakya
details: No hurtful truth, no pleasing lie
वचने का दरिद्रता — kind words are free

branches.label: वाक्क्षतम् — Vidura's warning
details: The wound of a harsh word never heals
Hence संयमः — restraint of the tongue

sections.heading: The title and the four ideals of speech
bullets: वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् means 'truth is the ornament of speech': वाचाम् is the genitive plural of वाक् (speech) and मण्डनम् means ornament.
The chapter teaches four ideals of noble speech: सत्यम् (truthfulness), माधुर्यम् (sweetness), हितम् (helpfulness) and संयमः (restraint).
The verses come from public-domain classics: भर्तृहरि's नीतिशतकम्, मनुस्मृतिः, चाणक्यनीतिः, श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता (17.15) and विदुरनीतिः.

sections.heading: Bhartrhari — speech as the lasting ornament
bullets: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम्...: armlets, moon-bright necklaces, bath, sandal-paste, flowers and dressed hair do not truly adorn a person.
वाणी एका समलङ्करोति: refined, cultured speech (संस्कृता वाणी) alone fully adorns.
क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि: all external ornaments wear away; वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् — the ornament of speech is the ornament forever.
The verse is from the नीतिशतकम् of भर्तृहरि and gives the chapter its central idea.

sections.heading: Manu and Chanakya — truth balanced with sweetness
bullets: मनु's fourfold rule: speak the truth, speak pleasantly, do not speak a hurtful truth, never speak a pleasing lie — एष धर्मः सनातनः.
Truth without kindness wounds; sweetness without truth is flattery — noble speech must be both true and kind.
चाणक्य: प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः — the gift of kind words delights every living being.
वचने का दरिद्रता — kind words cost nothing, so miserliness in speech is a strange poverty.

sections.heading: The Gita and Vidura — discipline and danger of the tongue
bullets: गीता 17.15 defines वाङ्मयं तपः by four marks: अनुद्वेगकरम् (non-agitating), सत्यम् (true), प्रियम् (pleasant), हितम् (beneficial), plus स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् (daily self-study).
The सुभाषित assigns each limb its moral jewel: हस्तस्य भूषणं दानम्, सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम्, श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं शास्त्रम्.
विदुर warns: wounds of arrows heal and felled forests regrow, but the wound of a harsh word (वाक्क्षतम्) never heals — न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्.
Therefore restraint (संयमः) is essential: a word once spoken, like an arrow shot, cannot be recalled.

sections.heading: Grammar from the verses
bullets: सन्धिः: चन्द्र + उज्ज्वलाः = चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः (गुण); न + अलङ्कृताः = नालङ्कृताः (दीर्घ); वाक् + भूषणम् = वाग्भूषणम् (जश्त्व); च + एव = चैव (वृद्धि); तपः + उच्यते = तप उच्यते (विसर्गलोप).
समासः: वाग्भूषणम् (षष्ठीतत्पुरुष), अनुद्वेगकरम् (नञ्), प्रियहितम् (द्वन्द्व), वाक्क्षतम् (तृतीयातत्पुरुष); वाङ्मयम् is वाक् + मयट् (तद्धित).
विभक्तिः: पुरुषम् (द्वितीया object), प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन / वाचा / सायकैः (तृतीया by), हस्तस्य / कण्ठस्य / वाचाम् (षष्ठी of), वचने (सप्तमी in).
Verb-forms: भूषयन्ति / तुष्यन्ति (लट्), ब्रूयात् (विधिलिङ् 'should speak'), धार्यते / उच्यते (passive), वक्तव्यम् (gerundive 'ought to be spoken').

key_takeaways: वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् — the true decoration of speech is truth, and refined speech is the lasting ornament of a person.
भर्तृहरि: all external ornaments perish (क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि); only cultured speech adorns forever — वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्.
मनु's eternal rule: speak the truth pleasantly; never a needlessly hurtful truth, never a pleasing lie.
चाणक्य: kind words are a free gift that delights all beings — why be a miser in speech (वचने का दरिद्रता)?
गीता 17.15: speech that is non-agitating, true, pleasant and beneficial, with daily self-study, is the austerity of speech (वाङ्मयं तपः).
विदुर: wounds of arrows heal, but the wound of a harsh word (वाक्क्षतम्) never heals — restrain the tongue.
From the verses we learn सन्धि (चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः, वाग्भूषणम्, चैव), समास (षष्ठीतत्पुरुष, नञ्, द्वन्द्व), विभक्ति roles and verb-forms (ब्रूयात्, उच्यते, वक्तव्यम्).

glossary.definition: Ornament, decoration; in the title वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् it names truth as the decoration of speech.
Speech, the faculty of the spoken word; वाचाम् is its genitive plural ('of words'), वाचा its instrumental ('by speech').
An armlet, an ornament worn on the upper arm; केयूराणि is its neuter plural in भर्तृहरि's verse.
Refined, polished, cultured speech — the one ornament that, per भर्तृहरि, truly and permanently adorns a person.
The ornament of speech (वाचः भूषणम्, षष्ठीतत्पुरुष compound); declared the only lasting ornament — वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्.
Falsehood, untruth; मनु forbids speaking even a pleasant falsehood (प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात्).
Eternal, ancient; मनु calls the fourfold rule of speech एष धर्मः सनातनः, the eternal law.
A pleasant, kind word; per चाणक्य its gift (प्रियवाक्यप्रदानम्) pleases all living beings.
Poverty, miserliness; वचने का दरिद्रता asks why one should be a miser with (free) kind words.
Not causing agitation or distress (नञ् compound of उद्वेगकर); the first mark of the Gita's austerity of speech.
The austerity of speech (गीता 17.15): speech non-agitating, true, pleasant and beneficial, joined with daily self-study.
Self-study, regular recitation and study of the scriptures; its practice (स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम्) completes the discipline of speech.
A wound made by words (वाचा क्षतम्); विदुर says such a wound, unlike arrow or axe wounds, never heals.
Restraint, self-control; applied to the tongue it means avoiding harsh, false and hurtful words.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 4)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses of the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate into simple English:
केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः
न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः ।
वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते
क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥
questions.answer: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor necklaces bright as the moon; neither bath nor sandal-paste, neither flowers nor elegantly dressed hair. Speech alone, when kept refined and cultured (संस्कृता वाणी), truly adorns a person. All (other) ornaments wear away (क्षीयन्ते); the ornament of speech is the ornament forever (वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्).
questions.explanation: भर्तृहरि's नीतिशतक verse: external ornaments perish; refined speech is the lasting ornament.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: केयूराणि, विलेपनम्, मूर्धजाः, क्षीयन्ते, संस्कृता.
questions.answer: केयूराणि = armlets (ornaments worn on the upper arm); विलेपनम् = sandal-paste / perfumed unguent; मूर्धजाः = hair (literally 'born of the head'); क्षीयन्ते = wear away, perish; संस्कृता = refined, polished, cultured.
questions.explanation: All five words occur in भर्तृहरि's verse केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति...

questions.question: मनु's rule ends 'एष धर्मः सनातनः'. State the four parts of this rule of speech and explain why it is called eternal.
questions.answer: The four parts: (1) speak the truth (सत्यं ब्रूयात्); (2) speak what is pleasant (प्रियं ब्रूयात्); (3) do not speak a hurtful truth (न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम्); (4) do not speak a pleasing falsehood (प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात्). It is called सनातन (eternal) because the balance of truth and kindness holds good in every age and society — it is a permanent law of noble conduct, not a passing custom.
questions.explanation: The verse balances सत्यम् with माधुर्यम् — both truth and sweetness are required.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) and name the sandhi: (a) वाग्भूषणम् (b) चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः.
questions.answer: (a) वाग्भूषणम् = वाक् + भूषणम् — जश्त्वसन्धिः (the क् becomes ग् before the voiced भ्). (b) चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः = चन्द्र + उज्ज्वलाः — गुणसन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ).
questions.explanation: Both forms occur in भर्तृहरि's verse; splitting them back is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: According to गीता 17.15, what four qualities must speech have to be called वाङ्मयं तपः, and what practice accompanies them?
questions.answer: Speech must be (1) अनुद्वेगकरम् — causing no agitation or distress; (2) सत्यम् — true; (3) प्रियम् — pleasant; and (4) हितम् — beneficial. Accompanying practice: स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् — the regular practice of self-study / recitation. Together these are called the austerity of speech (वाङ्मयं तपः).
questions.explanation: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्, स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते.

questions.question: 'वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम्' — Using at least three verses from the lesson, write an essay evaluating why the poets call truthful, refined speech the true ornament of a person, greater than physical ornaments.
questions.answer: भर्तृहरि (केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति...) argues that armlets, necklaces, baths, perfumes and flowers cannot really adorn a person because they are external and perishable — क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि. Only संस्कृता वाणी, refined and cultured speech, adorns permanently: वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्. The सुभाषित हस्तस्य भूषणं दानम्... deepens this: each limb has a moral jewel — charity for the hand, truth for the throat (सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम्), learning for the ear — so with such ornaments, other jewellery is pointless (भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम्). मनु adds the ethical core: speech is beautiful only when truth and kindness are balanced — no hurtful truth, no pleasing lie. And विदुर shows the negative proof: a harsh word wounds forever (न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्), so ill speech can disfigure a person more than any missing jewel. Evaluation: physical ornaments decorate only the body, can be bought, stolen and worn out, and say nothing of character; truthful sweet speech reveals inner culture, benefits the listener, wins lasting trust and cannot be taken away. Hence truth is rightly called the ornament of speech, and such speech the lasting ornament of the human being.
questions.explanation: A full answer cites भर्तृहरि, the भूषण subhashita, मनु and विदुर, and ends with the student's own evaluation.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) on मधुरा वाणी (sweet speech), and give the English meaning of each.
questions.answer:
1. मधुरा वाणी सर्वान् तोषयति। (Sweet speech pleases everyone.)
2. सत्यं वाचः भूषणम् अस्ति। (Truth is the ornament of speech.)
3. छात्रः कदापि कठोरं वचनं न वदेत्। (A student should never speak a harsh word.)
Together these say: speak sweetly and truthfully, and avoid harshness — for kind words please all beings and truth adorns speech.
questions.explanation: Simple sentences using chapter vocabulary; वदेत् is विधिलिङ् like ब्रूयात्.

questions.question: Translate 'प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः । तस्मात्तदेव वक्तव्यं वचने का दरिद्रता ॥' and state its moral.
questions.answer: Translation: By the gift of pleasant words all living beings are pleased; therefore pleasant (words) alone should be spoken — what poverty (can there be) in speech? Moral: kind words cost nothing yet delight everyone, so one should never be a miser with sweet speech.
questions.explanation: चाणक्य's verse: sweetness in speech is a free gift (प्रदानम्) available to all.

questions.question: Explain विदुर's image in 'रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् । वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् ॥'. What does it teach about harsh words?
questions.answer: A body pierced by arrows (सायकैः विद्धम्) heals, and even a forest felled by the axe (परशुना हतम्) grows again; but the ugly wound made by a harshly spoken word (वाक्क्षतम्) never heals over (न संरोहति). It teaches that words can hurt more deeply and more permanently than weapons, so the tongue must be restrained — a word once spoken cannot be recalled.
questions.explanation: The contrast between healing physical wounds and the unhealing word-wound argues for संयम of speech.

questions.question: Identify the form: (a) ब्रूयात् — which लकार and what does it express? (b) उच्यते — which voice and meaning?
questions.answer: (a) ब्रूयात् is विधिलिङ् लकार (optative) of the root ब्रू — it expresses 'should/ought to': 'one should speak'. (b) उच्यते is कर्मवाच्य (passive voice), लट् लकार, of वच् — 'is said / is called'.
questions.explanation: ब्रूयात् appears in मनु's verse; उच्यते in गीता 17.15 (वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते).

questions.question: The chapter title 'वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम्' means
options: truth is the ornament of speech
speech is the enemy of truth
wealth is the ornament of man
questions.answer: truth is the ornament of speech
questions.explanation: वाचाम् = of words/speech; मण्डनम् = ornament; सत्यम् = truth.

questions.question: The word 'मण्डनम्' means
questions.explanation: मण्डनम् = ornament/decoration, from the root मण्ड् (to adorn).

questions.question: In the title वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम्, the word वाचाम् is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: वाचाम् is the genitive plural of वाक् — 'of words'.

questions.question: Which set correctly lists the four ideals of noble speech taught in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Truthfulness, sweetness, benefit and restraint are the chapter's four ideals of speech.

questions.question: According to this chapter, the chief quality that adorns speech is
questions.explanation: The title itself declares truth (सत्यम्) to be the ornament of speech.

questions.question: The word 'वाक्' means
questions.explanation: वाक् (feminine) = speech, word; its forms include वाणी, वाचा, वाचाम्.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for falsehood, the opposite of सत्यम्, used in मनु's verse is
questions.explanation: अनृतम् = falsehood (न + ऋतम्); note the contrast with अमृतम् (nectar).

questions.question: 'मधुरा वाणी' means
questions.explanation: मधुरा = sweet; वाणी = speech. Sweetness of speech is माधुर्यम्.

questions.question: In भर्तृहरि's verse, 'केयूराणि' means
questions.explanation: केयूरम् is an armlet worn on the upper arm; केयूराणि is the plural.

questions.question: The verse 'केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम्...' was composed by
questions.explanation: It is a famous verse of भर्तृहरि from his नीतिशतकम्.

questions.question: भर्तृहरि's verse on वाग्भूषणम् is found in which work?
questions.explanation: The Nitishataka (century of verses on right conduct) contains this verse.

questions.question: In the verse, the adjective 'चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः' (bright as the moon) describes
questions.explanation: हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः — nor do moon-bright necklaces adorn a person.

questions.question: According to भर्तृहरि, what alone truly adorns a person?
questions.explanation: वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते — refined speech alone fully adorns.

questions.question: 'क्षीयन्ते' in क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि means
questions.explanation: क्षीयन्ते (from क्षि, to decay) — ornaments wear away with time.

questions.question: 'वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्' means
options: the ornament of speech is the (real) ornament
questions.answer: the ornament of speech is the (real) ornament
questions.explanation: While other ornaments perish, the ornament that is refined speech lasts forever.

questions.question: 'मूर्धजाः' literally means 'born of the head' and refers to
questions.explanation: मूर्धन् (head) + ज (born) — hair; नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः = nor well-dressed hair.

questions.question: 'विलेपनम्' in the verse means
questions.explanation: विलेपनम् = an unguent/paste (such as sandal) applied to the body.

questions.question: In 'या संस्कृता धार्यते', the relative pronoun या refers to
questions.explanation: The speech which is kept refined (संस्कृता) is the one ornament that adorns.

questions.question: 'सततम्' in सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् means
questions.explanation: सततम् = constantly, forever — the speech-ornament endures at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed by भर्तृहरि among the external adornments that fail to adorn a person?
questions.explanation: The verse lists केयूर, हार, स्नान, विलेपन, कुसुम and मूर्धजाः — earrings are not mentioned.

questions.question: 'समलङ्करोति' means
questions.explanation: सम् + अलङ्करोति = adorns well/fully; its subject is वाणी एका.

questions.question: The central message of भर्तृहरि's verse is that
options: outer ornaments perish, refined speech is the lasting ornament
one should buy the best ornaments available
bathing daily is the key to beauty
hair must always be decorated with flowers
questions.answer: outer ornaments perish, refined speech is the lasting ornament
questions.explanation: क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् sums up the message.

questions.question: The verse 'सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात्...' comes from
questions.explanation: It is the famous rule of speech from the मनुस्मृति (4.138).

questions.question: 'ब्रूयात्' means
questions.explanation: ब्रूयात् is the optative (विधिलिङ्) of ब्रू — 'one should speak'.

questions.question: According to मनु, what should NOT be spoken even though it is true?
options: a truth that is needlessly hurtful (सत्यम् अप्रियम्)
questions.answer: a truth that is needlessly hurtful (सत्यम् अप्रियम्)
questions.explanation: न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् — an unpleasant, wounding truth should not be blurted out.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नानृतम्' is
questions.explanation: न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः) — 'not... a falsehood'.

questions.question: 'अनृतम्' means
questions.explanation: अनृतम् = untruth/falsehood; distinguish from अमृतम् (nectar) and ऋतम् (cosmic truth).

questions.question: 'सनातनः' in एष धर्मः सनातनः means
questions.explanation: सनातन = eternal, ancient; the rule of speech is an everlasting law.

questions.question: 'प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात्' forbids
options: speaking a falsehood merely because it pleases
questions.answer: speaking a falsehood merely because it pleases
questions.explanation: Even a pleasing lie (प्रियम् अनृतम्) is forbidden — sweetness must never become flattery.

questions.question: मनु's verse essentially teaches the balance of
questions.explanation: सत्यम् must be joined with प्रियम् — truth spoken kindly, kindness kept truthful.

questions.question: 'अप्रियम्' means
questions.explanation: अ + प्रियम् = not pleasant, hurtful.

questions.question: In मनु's verse, 'प्रियम्' means
questions.explanation: प्रियम् = pleasing/agreeable — the quality that must accompany truth.

questions.question: 'प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति ____ ।' — the missing word is
questions.explanation: सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः — all living beings are pleased by kind words.

questions.question: 'तुष्यन्ति' means
questions.explanation: तुष्यन्ति (from तुष्, to be satisfied) = are pleased/contented.

questions.question: 'वचने का दरिद्रता' means
options: why be a miser in speech?
questions.answer: why be a miser in speech?
questions.explanation: Since kind words cost nothing, what poverty can there be in speech?

questions.question: 'दरिद्रता' means
questions.explanation: दरिद्रता = poverty/miserliness; here, stinginess with kind words.

questions.question: 'वक्तव्यम्' in तस्मात्तदेव वक्तव्यम् is
questions.explanation: वच् + तव्यत् gives the कृत्य form वक्तव्यम् — 'ought to be spoken'.

questions.question: The message of चाणक्य's verse प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन... is
options: kind words are a free gift that delights all beings
gifts of money are better than words
one should speak as little as possible
questions.answer: kind words are a free gift that delights all beings
questions.explanation: Sweet speech costs nothing yet pleases everyone — so never be stingy with it.

questions.question: 'जन्तवः' means
questions.explanation: जन्तुः = a living being/creature; जन्तवः is the nominative plural.

questions.question: 'प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन' is in which विभक्ति, and with what sense?
questions.explanation: The -एन ending marks the instrumental: beings are pleased BY the gift of kind words.

questions.question: The verse 'अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यम्...' (गीता 17.15) defines
options: शारीरं तपः (the austerity of the body)
मानसं तपः (the austerity of the mind)
questions.explanation: The verse ends वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते — 'this is called the austerity of speech'.

questions.question: 'अनुद्वेगकरम्' means speech that
questions.explanation: अन् (not) + उद्वेगकर (agitation-causing) — speech that disturbs no one.

questions.question: Which set gives the four marks of speech in गीता 17.15?
questions.explanation: Non-agitating, true, pleasant and beneficial — the four marks of disciplined speech.

questions.question: 'स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम्' in the verse means
options: the regular practice of self-study / scriptural recitation
questions.answer: the regular practice of self-study / scriptural recitation
questions.explanation: स्वाध्याय (self-study) + अभ्यसनम् (repeated practice) completes the speech-discipline.

questions.question: 'उच्यते' in वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते is
questions.explanation: उच्यते is the कर्मवाच्य (passive) लट् form of वच् — 'is said/called'.

questions.question: 'वाङ्मयम्' is formed as
questions.explanation: क् becomes ङ् before the nasal म (परसवर्ण); मयट् means 'made of' — 'consisting of speech'.

questions.question: The verse अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यम्... occurs in which chapter of the भगवद्गीता?
questions.explanation: It is verse 17.15, in the chapter on the three kinds of śraddhā and tapas.

questions.question: 'हितम्' means
questions.explanation: हितम् = good for, beneficial; speech should serve the listener's welfare.

questions.question: A remark that is true but deliberately humiliating fails which mark of वाङ्मयं तपः most directly?
questions.explanation: Being true, it satisfies सत्यम्; but by causing distress it violates अनुद्वेगकरम् (and हितम्).

questions.question: In गीता 17.15, 'तपः' is best translated as
questions.explanation: तपस् here means a practised discipline; speech itself becomes a form of tapas.

questions.question: 'हस्तस्य भूषणं ____' — the missing word in the सुभाषित is
questions.explanation: The ornament of the hand is charity (दानम्), not bracelets.

questions.question: According to the सुभाषित, the ornament of the throat (कण्ठस्य भूषणम्) is
questions.explanation: सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् — truth, not a necklace, adorns the throat.

questions.question: According to the सुभाषित, the ornament of the ear (श्रोत्रस्य भूषणम्) is
questions.explanation: श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं शास्त्रम् — listening to learning/scripture adorns the ear, not earrings.

questions.question: 'भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम्' means
questions.explanation: When the limbs wear moral jewels (दान, सत्य, शास्त्र), physical jewellery is pointless.

questions.question: 'श्रोत्रम्' means
questions.explanation: श्रोत्रम् = the ear (from श्रु, to hear); श्रोत्रस्य is its genitive.

questions.question: 'कण्ठः' means
questions.explanation: कण्ठः = throat/voice; कण्ठस्य भूषणम् = the ornament of the throat.

questions.question: The सुभाषित हस्तस्य भूषणं दानम्... teaches that
options: the real ornaments of the body are virtues, not jewels
each limb should wear one jewel
the hand is more important than the ear
questions.answer: the real ornaments of the body are virtues, not jewels
questions.explanation: Charity, truth and learning — one virtue-jewel for each limb — replace physical ornaments.

questions.question: In विदुर's verse, 'रोहते' means
questions.explanation: रुह् (to grow): the arrow-pierced body heals, the felled forest regrows.

questions.question: 'सायकैः' means
questions.explanation: सायकः = arrow; सायकैः is the instrumental plural — 'pierced BY arrows'.

questions.question: 'परशुना' means
questions.explanation: परशुः = axe; परशुना is the instrumental singular — 'cut down BY the axe'.

questions.question: 'वाक्क्षतम्' means
questions.explanation: वाचा क्षतम् — the injury inflicted by speech; a तृतीयातत्पुरुष compound.

questions.question: According to विदुर, which wound never heals?
options: the wound made by a harsh word
the wound made by an arrow
the wound made by an axe
questions.answer: the wound made by a harsh word
questions.explanation: न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् — arrow and axe wounds heal; the word-wound does not.

questions.question: 'दुरुक्तम्' in the verse means
questions.explanation: दुर् (badly) + उक्तम् (spoken) — a harshly uttered word; बीभत्सम् adds 'ugly, cruel'.

questions.question: The verse रोहते सायकैर्विद्धम्... comes from
questions.explanation: It is from विदुर's counsel to धृतराष्ट्र in the उद्योगपर्व of the महाभारत.

questions.question: 'चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः' is formed by which सन्धि?
questions.explanation: चन्द्र + उज्ज्वलाः: the final अ and initial उ combine into ओ — guṇa sandhi.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'वाग्भूषणम्' is
questions.explanation: The base word is वाक्; क् becomes ग् before the voiced भ् (जश्त्वसन्धिः).

questions.question: 'वाग्भूषणम्' (वाचः भूषणम् — 'the ornament OF speech') is which समास?
questions.explanation: The first member stands in the genitive relation ('of speech') — a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष compound.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नालङ्कृताः' is
questions.explanation: न + अलङ्कृताः = नालङ्कृताः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः) — 'nor adorned (hair)'.

questions.question: 'ब्रूयात्' is in which लकार?
questions.explanation: The optative (विधिलिङ्) expresses 'should': सत्यं ब्रूयात् — one should speak the truth.

questions.question: 'तुष्यन्ति' is in which लकार?
questions.explanation: तुष्यन्ति is present tense, third person plural — '(they) are pleased'.

questions.question: 'वचने' (in वचने का दरिद्रता) is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: वचने is locative singular — 'IN speech, what poverty?'

questions.question: 'हस्तस्य' (of the hand) is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: The -स्य ending marks the genitive singular — 'OF the hand'.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'चैव' is
questions.explanation: च + एव = चैव (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धिः).

questions.question: 'अनुद्वेगकरम्' contains which negative element?
questions.explanation: न + उद्वेगकरम् → अनुद्वेगकरम्: the नञ् negative appears as अन् before the vowel उ.

questions.question: In 'वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते', the form तप (for तपः) results from
options: विसर्गलोपः — the visarga is dropped before the vowel उ
questions.answer: विसर्गलोपः — the visarga is dropped before the vowel उ
questions.explanation: तपः + उच्यते → तप उच्यते: the visarga of तपः is elided before उ.

questions.question: The line 'वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्' occurs in भर्तृहरि's नीतिशतकम्.
questions.explanation: It is the closing phrase of the नीतिशतक verse केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति...

questions.question: According to मनु, an unpleasant (hurtful) truth should always be spoken openly.
questions.explanation: मनु says न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् — one should NOT speak a needlessly hurtful truth.

questions.question: The verb 'तुष्यन्ति' is in लट् लकार (present tense).
questions.explanation: तुष्यन्ति is present tense, third person plural of तुष् — 'are pleased'.

questions.question: According to विदुरनीति, a wound made by harsh words (वाक्क्षतम्) heals quickly.
questions.explanation: न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् — the word-wound never heals, unlike arrow and axe wounds.

questions.question: गीता 17.15 includes speech that causes agitation (उद्वेगकरम्) within the austerity of speech.
questions.explanation: The first mark is अनुद्वेगकरम् — speech must NOT cause agitation or distress.

questions.question: 'वाग्भूषणम्' is a षष्ठीतत्पुरुष compound meaning 'the ornament of speech'.
questions.explanation: वाचः भूषणम् — the first member carries a genitive sense, so it is षष्ठीतत्पुरुष.

questions.question: According to चाणक्य, speaking kind words costs nothing.
questions.explanation: वचने का दरिद्रता — there is no poverty in speech; kind words are a free gift.

questions.question: The word 'सनातनः' means 'new, recent'.
questions.explanation: सनातनः means eternal, ancient — एष धर्मः सनातनः, 'this is the eternal law'.

questions.question: According to the सुभाषित, the ornament of the throat is truth (सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम्).
questions.explanation: हस्तस्य भूषणं दानं सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् — truth adorns the throat.

questions.question: The verb 'उच्यते' is in the active voice.
questions.explanation: उच्यते is कर्मवाच्य (passive) — 'is called', not 'calls'.

questions.question: वाचां मण्डनं ____ । (Complete the chapter's title phrase.)
questions.explanation: वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम् — truth is the ornament of speech.

questions.question: सत्यं ब्रूयात् ____ ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् ।
questions.explanation: सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् — speak the truth, speak the pleasant.

questions.question: क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं ____ ।
questions.explanation: वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् — the ornament of speech is the (real) ornament.

questions.question: प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे ____ जन्तवः ।
questions.explanation: All living beings ARE PLEASED (तुष्यन्ति) by the gift of kind words.

questions.question: तस्मात्तदेव वक्तव्यं वचने का ____ ।
questions.explanation: वचने का दरिद्रता — what poverty (can there be) in speech?

questions.question: अनुद्वेगकरं ____ सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । (गीता 17.15)
questions.explanation: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यम् — speech that causes no agitation.

questions.question: स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं ____ उच्यते ।
questions.explanation: वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते — (this) is called the austerity of speech. (Base form: तपः)

questions.question: हस्तस्य भूषणं ____ सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् ।
questions.explanation: The ornament of the hand is charity (दानम्).

questions.question: हस्तस्य भूषणं दानं सत्यं ____ भूषणम् ।
questions.explanation: सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् — truth is the ornament OF THE THROAT.

questions.question: श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं ____ भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम् ।
questions.explanation: श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं शास्त्रम् — learning is the ornament of the ear.

questions.question: वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति ____ ।
questions.explanation: The wound made by words (वाक्क्षतम्) never heals over.

questions.question: प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष ____ सनातनः ।
questions.explanation: एष धर्मः सनातनः — this is the eternal law.

questions.question: क्षीयन्ते खलु ____ सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ।
questions.explanation: क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि — (other) ornaments indeed wear away.

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत (join): न + अनृतम् = ____ ।
questions.explanation: न + अनृतम् = नानृतम् (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घसन्धिः).

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत (join): वाक् + भूषणम् = ____ ।
questions.explanation: क् becomes ग् before the voiced भ् (जश्त्वसन्धिः): वाग्भूषणम्.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the chapter title 'वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम्', analysing each word.
questions.answer: वाचाम् = 'of words/speech' (genitive plural of वाक्); मण्डनम् = ornament, decoration; सत्यम् = truth. The phrase therefore means 'truth is the ornament of speech' — what truly decorates our words is not cleverness or loudness but truthfulness.
questions.explanation: The title states the chapter's central idea: speech is beautified by truth.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय (prose order) of भर्तृहरि's verse 'केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम्...' and give its gist in one sentence.
questions.answer: अन्वय: केयूराणि पुरुषं न भूषयन्ति, चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः हाराः न (भूषयन्ति), न स्नानम्, न विलेपनम्, न कुसुमम्, न अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः (भूषयन्ति)। या संस्कृता (वाणी) धार्यते, (सा) एका वाणी पुरुषं समलङ्करोति। भूषणानि खलु क्षीयन्ते; वाग्भूषणं सततं भूषणम्। Gist: no external ornament adorns a person — only refined speech does, and it alone lasts forever.
questions.explanation: The अन्वय rearranges the verse into natural prose order for easy construal.

questions.question: According to भर्तृहरि, why do physical ornaments fail to truly adorn a person?
questions.answer: Because they are external and perishable — क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि, ornaments wear away, break and fade with time. They can also be bought or stolen, so they say nothing about the person's inner worth. Refined speech (संस्कृता वाणी), by contrast, is an inner quality that endures always (सततम्).
questions.explanation: The contrast is between perishable outer decoration and imperishable inner culture.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: हाराः, कुसुमम्, खलु, सततम्, धार्यते.
questions.answer: हाराः = necklaces; कुसुमम् = flower; खलु = indeed, certainly; सततम् = always, constantly; धार्यते = is maintained/borne (passive of धृ).
questions.explanation: All five occur in भर्तृहरि's verse on the ornament of speech.

questions.question: State मनु's four-part rule of speech (मनुस्मृति 4.138) and explain the logic connecting the four parts.
questions.answer: (1) सत्यं ब्रूयात् — speak the truth; (2) प्रियं ब्रूयात् — speak pleasantly; (3) न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् — do not speak a needlessly hurtful truth; (4) प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् — do not speak a pleasing falsehood. Logic: the first two set the two ideals (truth, sweetness); the last two guard against misusing one ideal to violate the other — truth must not become cruelty, and sweetness must not become lying. Only speech that is both true and kind satisfies the eternal law (एष धर्मः सनातनः).
questions.explanation: The rule is a complete system: two positive commands and two prohibitions that balance each other.

questions.question: If मनु forbids the hurtful truth, does he permit lying to avoid hurting someone? Explain with the verse.
questions.answer: No. The very next line — प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् — forbids speaking even a pleasant falsehood. मनु's solution is not to lie but to choose silence or a gentle, tactful wording when a truth can only wound and cannot help. Truth remains compulsory; only its needlessly cruel expression is barred.
questions.explanation: The two prohibitions work together: no cruel truth, no kind lie — hence gentle truth or restraint.

questions.question: Translate: प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः । तस्मात्तदेव वक्तव्यं वचने का दरिद्रता ॥
questions.answer: By the gift of pleasant words all living beings are pleased; therefore that (pleasant word) alone should be spoken — what poverty (can there be) in speech?
questions.explanation: चाणक्य's verse: kind words are free, so one should never be a miser with them.

questions.question: 'वचने का दरिद्रता' is a rhetorical question. What does it imply about people who speak rudely?
questions.answer: It implies that rudeness is a self-imposed and absurd poverty. Kind words cost nothing — they are an inexhaustible wealth available to everyone. A person who cannot 'afford' a kind word behaves like a miser hoarding a treasure that never diminishes; his poverty is of the heart and tongue, not of the purse.
questions.explanation: The rhetorical question exposes rudeness as pointless stinginess in something that is free.

questions.question: List the four marks of speech and the accompanying practice that together constitute वाङ्मयं तपः (गीता 17.15).
questions.answer: The four marks: (1) अनुद्वेगकरम् — causing no agitation; (2) सत्यम् — true; (3) प्रियम् — pleasant; (4) हितम् — beneficial. Accompanying practice: स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् — the regular practice of self-study/recitation. Together these are called the austerity of speech.
questions.explanation: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्, स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते।

questions.question: Why does the गीता classify disciplined speech as a form of तपस् (austerity) rather than mere good manners?
questions.answer: Because controlling the tongue demands constant inner effort — like fasting or meditation, it disciplines an impulse (the urge to blurt, boast, wound or lie). Speech that is simultaneously non-agitating, true, pleasant and beneficial cannot be produced by etiquette alone; it requires mastery over anger, ego and carelessness. Joined with daily स्वाध्याय, it purifies the speaker himself, which is the very purpose of tapas. Hence the tongue becomes an instrument of self-cultivation, not just social politeness.
questions.explanation: Tapas = sustained self-discipline; the four marks demand exactly that from the speaker.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: अनुद्वेगकरम्, स्वाध्यायः, हितम्, उच्यते.
questions.answer: अनुद्वेगकरम् = not causing agitation/distress; स्वाध्यायः = self-study, recitation of scripture; हितम् = beneficial, good (for the listener); उच्यते = is called/said (passive).
questions.explanation: All four occur in गीता 17.15 defining the austerity of speech.

questions.question: According to the सुभाषित 'हस्तस्य भूषणं दानम्...', state the true ornament of each: the hand, the throat, the ear.
questions.answer: The hand's ornament is दानम् (charity/giving); the throat's ornament is सत्यम् (truth); the ear's ornament is शास्त्रम् (learning/listening to wisdom). With these, the verse asks, what use are other ornaments (भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम्)?
questions.explanation: Each limb receives a moral jewel in place of a physical one.

questions.question: Translate विदुर's verse: रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् । वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् ॥
questions.answer: That which is pierced by arrows heals, and a forest cut down by the axe grows again; but the ugly (wound of a) harshly spoken word — the wound made by speech (वाक्क्षतम्) — never heals over.
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts healing physical wounds with the permanent wound of cruel words.

questions.question: Why does विदुर consider the word-wound (वाक्क्षतम्) worse than the arrow-wound? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: (1) Permanence: the arrow-wound closes with time, but the insult lodges in the memory and heart — न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम्, it never heals. (2) Irrevocability: like an arrow already shot, a word once uttered cannot be recalled, and unlike a physical wound it can be reopened every time the victim remembers it. Hence the tongue needs stricter restraint than any weapon.
questions.explanation: The comparison argues for संयम (restraint) as the highest discipline of speech.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) चैव (b) तस्मात्तदेव.
questions.answer: (a) चैव = च + एव — वृद्धिसन्धिः (अ + ए = ऐ). (b) तस्मात्तदेव = तस्मात् + तत् + एव — the final त् of तस्मात् doubles before त, and तत् + एव becomes तदेव (त् becomes द् before the vowel — व्यञ्जनसन्धिः).
questions.explanation: Both forms occur in the chapter's verses (गीता 17.15 and चाणक्य's verse).

questions.question: Explain the formation of (a) वाङ्मयम् and (b) the phrase तप उच्यते (for तपः + उच्यते).
questions.answer: (a) वाङ्मयम् = वाक् + मयट् (the तद्धित suffix मय, 'consisting of'): the क् of वाक् becomes the nasal ङ् before म् (परसवर्ण/अनुनासिक change) — 'consisting of speech'. (b) तपः + उच्यते → तप उच्यते by विसर्गलोपः: the visarga of तपः is dropped before the vowel उ.
questions.explanation: Both occur in the closing line of गीता 17.15: वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते.

questions.question: Name the समास and give the विग्रह (analysis) of: वाग्भूषणम्, अनुद्वेगकरम्, प्रियहितम्.
questions.answer: वाग्भूषणम् = वाचः भूषणम् ('the ornament of speech') — षष्ठीतत्पुरुषः. अनुद्वेगकरम् = न उद्वेगकरम् ('not causing agitation') — नञ्समासः (नञ्तत्पुरुष; the negative appears as अन् before the vowel). प्रियहितम् = प्रियं च हितं च ('pleasant and beneficial') — द्वन्द्वसमासः.
questions.explanation: Three different compound types drawn from the chapter's verses.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति, वचन and sense of: सायकैः, परशुना, वाचा (from विदुर's verse).
questions.answer: सायकैः — तृतीया बहुवचन, 'by arrows'; परशुना — तृतीया एकवचन, 'by an axe'; वाचा — तृतीया एकवचन, 'by speech'. All three are instrumentals naming the instrument that inflicts the wound.
questions.explanation: The instrumental (तृतीया) systematically marks the wounding instrument in the verse.

questions.question: Identify the form (लकार / voice) of: भूषयन्ति, ब्रूयात्, धार्यते.
questions.answer: भूषयन्ति — लट् लकार (present), third person plural, active: '(they) adorn'. ब्रूयात् — विधिलिङ् (optative), third person singular: 'one should speak'. धार्यते — कर्मवाच्य (passive), लट्, third person singular: 'is maintained/borne'.
questions.explanation: Three different verb-forms from भर्तृहरि's and मनु's verses.

questions.question: Name the four ideals of noble speech taught by this chapter and give a one-line meaning of each.
questions.answer: (1) सत्यम् — truthfulness: never speak what is false. (2) माधुर्यम् — sweetness: speak gently and pleasantly (मधुरा वाणी). (3) हितम् — benefit: let speech serve the listener's good. (4) संयमः — restraint: hold back harsh, cruel and careless words.
questions.explanation: The four ideals summarise भर्तृहरि, मनु, चाणक्य, the गीता and विदुर together.

questions.question: Your friend has performed poorly in an examination and asks for your opinion on his answer sheet. Applying मनु's rule of speech, what should you say and what should you avoid?
questions.answer: Apply the four parts: speak the truth — do not pretend the paper is excellent (that would be प्रियम् अनृतम्, a pleasing lie, which मनु forbids). But avoid the needlessly hurtful truth (सत्यम् अप्रियम्) — do not mock or say 'you are hopeless'. The right course: state the weaknesses honestly but gently and helpfully (सत्यं प्रियं च) — e.g. point out exactly where marks were lost, praise what was done well, and suggest how to improve. Thus truth is preserved, kindness is preserved, and the speech is also हितम् (beneficial).
questions.explanation: The scenario tests the balance: no flattery, no cruelty — gentle, useful truth.

questions.question: Write from memory any one complete verse of this chapter on speech, and name its source.
questions.answer: Example: सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् । प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः ॥ — Source: मनुस्मृतिः (4.138). (Any other chapter verse with its correct source — भर्तृहरि's नीतिशतकम्, चाणक्यनीतिः, भगवद्गीता 17.15, or विदुरनीतिः — is acceptable.)
questions.explanation: Any verse of the lesson, quoted accurately with its source, earns full marks.

questions.question: Explain भर्तृहरि's verse 'केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम्...' in detail: give the शब्दार्थ of its key words, the अन्वय, an English translation, and its message.
questions.answer: शब्दार्थ: केयूराणि = armlets; हाराः चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः = moon-bright necklaces; स्नानम् = bath; विलेपनम् = sandal-paste; कुसुमम् = flower; अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः = dressed hair; वाणी एका = speech alone; संस्कृता = refined; धार्यते = is maintained; क्षीयन्ते = perish; सततम् = forever. अन्वय: केयूराणि पुरुषं न भूषयन्ति, चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः हाराः न, न स्नानम्, न विलेपनम्, न कुसुमम्, न अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः; या संस्कृता (वाणी) धार्यते, सा एका वाणी पुरुषं समलङ्करोति; भूषणानि खलु क्षीयन्ते, वाग्भूषणं सततं भूषणम्। Translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor moon-bright necklaces, nor bath, sandal-paste, flowers or dressed hair; speech alone, kept refined, truly adorns a person; ornaments wear away — the ornament of speech is the ornament forever. Message: external beauty is borrowed and perishable; cultivated speech reveals inner culture, cannot be stolen or worn out, and is therefore the only lasting adornment — वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्.
questions.explanation: A complete verse-study: vocabulary, prose order, translation and moral.

questions.question: Compare मनु's rule of speech (सत्यं ब्रूयात्...) with the गीता's definition of वाङ्मयं तपः (17.15). What do they share, and what does each add?
questions.answer: Shared core: both demand that speech be simultaneously true (सत्यम्) and pleasant (प्रियम्) — truth alone is not enough; it must not wound. मनु's distinctive contribution: the two explicit prohibitions — never a hurtful truth, never a pleasing lie — which resolve the practical conflict between truth and kindness, and the claim that this balance is the eternal law (एष धर्मः सनातनः). The गीता's additions: (1) अनुद्वेगकरम् — a stricter psychological test: speech must not agitate anyone; (2) हितम् — speech must actively benefit the listener, not merely avoid harm; (3) स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् — the discipline extends to feeding the mind through daily study, since good speech flows from a well-nourished mind; (4) the framing of speech as तपस् — a spiritual austerity that purifies the speaker. Conclusion: मनु gives the ethical rule for individual utterances; the गीता turns the same values into a complete lifelong discipline of the tongue.
questions.explanation: Both texts balance truth and sweetness; Manu adds prohibitions, the Gita adds benefit, study and the tapas framing.

questions.question: In the age of social media, messages can be posted in a second and read by thousands. Evaluate how the teachings of this chapter (मनु, चाणक्य, गीता, विदुर) apply to online speech.
questions.answer: विदुर's warning applies with double force online: a cruel post is a वाक्क्षतम् that not only never heals but is also permanently recorded, searchable and shareable — the arrow, once shot, multiplies. मनु's rule gives the test before posting: is it true? is it kind? A hurtful truth (public shaming) and a pleasing falsehood (flattering fake news) are both forbidden. चाणक्य's वचने का दरिद्रता reminds us that encouraging comments cost nothing yet can lift thousands of readers — kindness scales as easily as cruelty. The गीता's four marks form a practical checklist for every post: अनुद्वेगकरम् (will it inflame or calm?), सत्यम् (is it verified?), प्रियम् (is the tone gentle?), हितम् (does it help anyone?), and स्वाध्याय suggests reading and learning before opining. Evaluation: the ancient principles transfer perfectly because the moral structure of speech is unchanged; only the reach has grown — which makes संयम (restraint: pausing before posting) more, not less, necessary today.
questions.explanation: A strong answer applies each source to a concrete online behaviour and ends with an evaluation.

questions.question: From the verses of this chapter, give five सन्धि examples, showing the split (विच्छेद) and naming the type of each.
questions.answer: (1) चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः = चन्द्र + उज्ज्वलाः — गुणसन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ). (2) नालङ्कृताः = न + अलङ्कृताः — दीर्घसन्धिः (अ + अ = आ); similarly नानृतम् = न + अनृतम्. (3) वाग्भूषणम् = वाक् + भूषणम् — जश्त्वसन्धिः (क् → ग् before the voiced भ्). (4) चैव = च + एव — वृद्धिसन्धिः (अ + ए = ऐ). (5) तप उच्यते = तपः + उच्यते — विसर्गसन्धिः (विसर्गलोपः before उ); compare सायकैर्विद्धम् = सायकैः + विद्धम्, where the visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound.
questions.explanation: Five distinct sandhi types — गुण, दीर्घ, जश्त्व, वृद्धि, विसर्ग — all drawn from the chapter.

questions.question: 'A wound from a sword heals; a wound from words does not.' Evaluate this claim of विदुरनीति with the verse रोहते सायकैर्विद्धम्..., giving arguments and one possible counter-argument with your response to it.
questions.answer: विदुर's claim rests on a real asymmetry. Arguments for: (1) physical wounds heal by natural processes, but an insult is stored in memory and re-felt each time it is recalled — the wound reopens indefinitely; (2) harsh words attack the self-respect, not the flesh, and self-respect has no bandage; (3) relationships broken by cruel speech often never recover, though bodies recover from grave injuries. Counter-argument: some say time heals emotional wounds too, and forgiveness can erase them, so the verse exaggerates. Response: the verse is deliberately hyperbolic to teach vigilance, yet experience supports its core — even after forgiveness, the memory of a बीभत्स word rarely vanishes, while a healed cut is truly forgotten. The exaggeration is thus morally accurate: since we cannot predict which word will wound forever, the only safe course is संयम — restraint before speaking. Conclusion: the claim is substantially valid as a guide to conduct.
questions.explanation: Evaluation with reasons, a counter-view and a reasoned verdict — senior-secondary level.

questions.question: Explain गीता 17.15 (अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यम्...) in detail: translation, the meaning of each of the four marks with an everyday example, and the role of स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम्.
questions.answer: Translation: 'Speech that causes no distress, that is true, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular practice of self-study — this is called the austerity of speech (वाङ्मयं तपः).' The four marks: (1) अनुद्वेगकरम् — not agitating: correcting a junior privately instead of shouting before others; (2) सत्यम् — true: refusing to spread an unverified rumour; (3) प्रियम् — pleasant: framing a request politely ('could you please...') rather than as a bark; (4) हितम् — beneficial: warning a friend about a bad habit because it helps him, not to score points. Role of स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम्: daily study and recitation feed the mind with noble matter, so the tongue has something worthy to utter — speech-discipline is completed by nourishing its source. Together these make the tongue an instrument of तपस्, purifying the speaker while protecting the listener.
questions.explanation: Each mark must be explained with a concrete example; स्वाध्याय supplies the positive content of speech.

questions.question: Compose a short Sanskrit paragraph of four or five simple sentences (in Devanagari) on the glory of speech (वाण्याः महिमा), using vocabulary from this chapter, and give its English translation.
questions.answer: Example: वाणी मनुष्यस्य सत्यं भूषणम् अस्ति। मधुरा वाणी सर्वान् जनान् तोषयति। सत्यं वदेत् प्रियं वदेत्। कठोरं वचनं वाक्क्षतं जनयति। तस्मात् वयं सदा संस्कृतां वाणीं धारयेम। Translation: Speech is the true ornament of a human being. Sweet speech pleases all people. One should speak the truth, one should speak pleasantly. A harsh word produces a word-wound. Therefore let us always maintain refined speech. (Any grammatically sound paragraph using chapter vocabulary — वाणी, सत्यम्, मधुरा, भूषणम्, वाक्क्षतम्, संस्कृता — deserves full marks.)
questions.explanation: Tests composition: simple लट्/विधिलिङ् sentences built from the chapter's word-stock.

questions.question: 'वाचां मण्डनं सत्यम्' — Using all the main verses of the chapter, write an essay on the ethics of speech in Sanskrit literature, covering the ornament-idea, the truth-sweetness balance, speech as discipline, and the danger of harsh words.
questions.answer: The ornament-idea: भर्तृहरि declares that armlets, necklaces, baths and flowers fail to adorn; only संस्कृता वाणी adorns, and unlike ornaments it never perishes — वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्. The सुभाषित extends this to every limb: दानम् for the hand, सत्यम् for the throat, शास्त्रम् for the ear. The truth-sweetness balance: मनु commands truth spoken pleasantly, forbidding both the wounding truth and the pleasing lie — एष धर्मः सनातनः; चाणक्य adds that kind words are a free gift that delights every creature (वचने का दरिद्रता). Speech as discipline: the गीता raises this ethic to तपस् — speech must be non-agitating, true, pleasant and beneficial, sustained by daily स्वाध्याय; the tongue thus becomes a means of self-purification. The danger: विदुर warns that wounds of arrows and axes heal but the वाक्क्षतम् never does, so restraint (संयमः) is the final guardian of speech. Conclusion: Sanskrit literature treats speech not as mere communication but as the visible form of character — its beauty is truth, its sweetness is compassion, its discipline is tapas, and its misuse is the one wound that cannot be undone.
questions.explanation: The model essay integrates all five sources under the chapter's four ideals.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः
न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः ।
वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते
क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥
(a) List any four external adornments the poet rejects. (b) What single thing truly adorns a person, and what condition must it satisfy? (c) What happens to ordinary ornaments, and what word expresses this? (d) Name the poet and his work.
questions.answer: (a) Any four of: केयूराणि (armlets), हाराः (necklaces), स्नानम् (bath), विलेपनम् (sandal-paste), कुसुमम् (flower), अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः (dressed hair). (b) वाणी — speech; it must be संस्कृता (refined, cultured) and constantly maintained (धार्यते). (c) They wear away/perish; the word is क्षीयन्ते. (d) भर्तृहरिः, in his नीतिशतकम्.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the chapter's central verse, tested part by part.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम् ।
प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः ॥
(a) What two positive commands does the verse give? (b) What two kinds of speech does it forbid? (c) Which word means 'falsehood', and what is its सन्धि-विच्छेद in नानृतम्? (d) Why is this rule called सनातन?
questions.answer: (a) Speak the truth (सत्यं ब्रूयात्) and speak what is pleasant (प्रियं ब्रूयात्). (b) It forbids the unpleasant/hurtful truth (सत्यम् अप्रियम्) and the pleasant falsehood (प्रियम् अनृतम्). (c) अनृतम् means falsehood; नानृतम् = न + अनृतम् (दीर्घसन्धिः). (d) Because the balance of truth and kindness is a permanent law of noble conduct valid in every age — hence एष धर्मः सनातनः, 'this is the eternal dharma'.
questions.explanation: The four-part structure and the दीर्घ sandhi are both tested from the quoted text.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः ।
तस्मात्तदेव वक्तव्यं वचने का दरिद्रता ॥
(a) By what are all beings pleased? (b) What does the rhetorical question वचने का दरिद्रता mean? (c) Identify the विभक्ति of प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन and its sense.
questions.answer: (a) By the gift of pleasant/kind words (प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन). (b) 'What poverty (can there be) in speech?' — kind words cost nothing, so there is no excuse for being miserly with them. (c) तृतीया (instrumental) एकवचन — 'BY the giving of pleasant words'.
questions.explanation: Meaning plus one grammar identification from चाणक्य's verse.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
(a) List the four qualities required of speech. (b) What additional practice is named? (c) What is such speech collectively called? (d) Give the सन्धि-विच्छेद of चैव and the समास type of अनुद्वेगकरम्.
questions.answer: (a) अनुद्वेगकरम् (non-agitating), सत्यम् (true), प्रियम् (pleasant) and हितम् (beneficial) — the last two joined in प्रियहितम्. (b) स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनम् — the regular practice of self-study/recitation. (c) वाङ्मयं तपः — the austerity of speech. (d) चैव = च + एव (वृद्धिसन्धिः); अनुद्वेगकरम् is a नञ्समास (न + उद्वेगकरम्, negative अन् before a vowel).
questions.explanation: Comprehension and grammar drawn directly from गीता 17.15.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् ।
वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् ॥
(a) What two kinds of wounds does the verse say CAN heal? (b) Which wound never heals? (c) State the विभक्ति shared by सायकैः, परशुना and वाचा, and its sense here. (d) What practical lesson does विदुर draw for us?
questions.answer: (a) The wound of one pierced by arrows (सायकैः विद्धम्) and the forest cut down by an axe (परशुना हतम्) — both grow/heal again (रोहते). (b) The वाक्क्षतम् — the ugly wound made by a harshly spoken word (वाचा दुरुक्तम्) — न संरोहति, it never heals. (c) All three are in तृतीया (instrumental), naming the instrument: 'by arrows', 'by an axe', 'by speech'. (d) Restrain the tongue (संयमः): think before speaking, for a word once released cannot be recalled and its wound is permanent.
questions.explanation: The instrumental series and the healing/non-healing contrast carry the verse's teaching.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
हस्तस्य भूषणं दानं सत्यं कण्ठस्य भूषणम् ।
श्रोत्रस्य भूषणं शास्त्रं भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम् ॥
(a) Match each limb with its true ornament. (b) What is the force of the final question भूषणैः किं प्रयोजनम्? (c) Which विभक्ति do हस्तस्य, कण्ठस्य and श्रोत्रस्य share?
questions.answer: (a) Hand (हस्तस्य) — charity (दानम्); throat (कण्ठस्य) — truth (सत्यम्); ear (श्रोत्रस्य) — learning (शास्त्रम्). (b) It is rhetorical: when the limbs already wear these moral jewels, physical ornaments serve no purpose at all. (c) All three are in षष्ठी (genitive) एकवचन — 'of the hand/throat/ear'.
questions.explanation: The verse restates the chapter's theme: virtues, not jewels, adorn the body.

questions.question:
Situation: In class, राहुल mocks a classmate's stammer in front of everyone, and the class laughs. The classmate stops answering questions for the rest of the term.
(a) Which verse of this chapter most directly explains the classmate's lasting silence? (b) Which quality of speech did राहुल violate according to गीता 17.15? (c) What should राहुल have done instead, according to चाणक्य?
questions.answer: (a) विदुर's verse रोहते सायकैर्विद्धम्... — the mockery inflicted a वाक्क्षतम्, a word-wound that does not heal, which is why the classmate remains withdrawn. (b) अनुद्वेगकरम् — his words caused agitation and humiliation (they were also neither प्रियम् nor हितम्). (c) चाणक्य teaches प्रियवाक्यप्रदानेन सर्वे तुष्यन्ति जन्तवः — kind words cost nothing; राहुल should have spoken encouragingly to the classmate, since there is no poverty in speech (वचने का दरिद्रता).
questions.explanation: Applies three sources of the chapter to one classroom incident.

questions.question:
Situation: A doctor must tell a patient's family that the illness is serious. She states the facts accurately, but calmly and gently, explains what can still be done, and answers every question patiently. A colleague says she should have simply declared the blunt prognosis and left.
(a) Whose conduct better follows मनु's rule of speech? Justify with the verse. (b) Which of the गीता's four marks does the doctor's speech satisfy? (c) Was the doctor obliged to hide the truth to be kind? Why not?
questions.answer: (a) The doctor's. मनु commands सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयात् — the truth must be spoken, but pleasantly; the colleague's blunt declaration is सत्यम् अप्रियम्, the needlessly harsh truth that मनु forbids (न ब्रूयात् सत्यमप्रियम्). (b) All four: her words are true (सत्यम्), gentle in manner (प्रियम्), aimed at the family's welfare and next steps (हितम्), and delivered calmly so as not to add panic (अनुद्वेगकरम्). (c) No. मनु equally forbids the pleasing falsehood (प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयात्); hiding the truth would be अनृतम्. The rule requires truthful content in a kind form — exactly what she did.
questions.explanation: The medical scenario tests the full four-part balance of truth and kindness.

questions.question:
Read this line from the chapter and answer the grammar questions:
'क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्'
(a) Give the सन्धि-विच्छेद of वाग्भूषणम् and name the सन्धि. (b) State the समास of वाग्भूषणम् with its विग्रह. (c) Identify the लकार and वचन of क्षीयन्ते. (d) What is the विभक्ति and वचन of भूषणानि?
questions.answer: (a) वाग्भूषणम् = वाक् + भूषणम् — जश्त्वसन्धिः (क् becomes ग् before the voiced भ्). (b) षष्ठीतत्पुरुषसमासः; विग्रह: वाचः भूषणम् — 'the ornament of speech'. (c) क्षीयन्ते is लट् लकार (present), third person बहुवचन (plural) — '(they) wear away'. (d) भूषणानि is प्रथमा (nominative) बहुवचन, neuter — the subject 'ornaments'.
questions.explanation: Four grammar identifications from a single quoted line.

questions.question:
Situation: Before posting an angry reply to a provocative message in the school group-chat, मीरा pauses and checks her draft against गीता 17.15. Her draft calls the sender a liar in insulting language, though her facts are correct.
(a) Which marks of वाङ्मयं तपः does the draft fail? (b) Does having correct facts make the post acceptable? (c) Rewrite the approach मीरा should take, in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: (a) It fails अनुद्वेगकरम् (it will inflame), प्रियम् (insulting tone) and हितम् (it helps no one) — it satisfies only सत्यम्. (b) No — the गीता requires all four marks together; truth delivered as an insult is still undisciplined speech, and मनु likewise forbids the hurtful truth. (c) She should state the correct facts calmly and politely, without name-calling — e.g. 'I think this claim is mistaken; here is the correct information' — so the message stays true, gentle, non-inflammatory and useful.
questions.explanation: The four marks work as a checklist; one mark alone (truth) is not sufficient.
